newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian bonds churn in familiar range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian bonds churn in familiar range.

text.p: *Australian bond futures churned in a four basis point trading range during SYCOM, remaining in familiar territory ahead of this week's key local and U.S. events.
*Local inflation data Wednesday, wages report Thursday.
Australian bond futures contracts churned in a four basis point trading range during SYCOM, remaining in familiar territory ahead of this week's key local and U.S. events.
The 10-year bond futures contract ended after hours trade at 93.425 compared with Monday's firm 93.445 pit close and after testing initial support at 93.410.
Peter Pontikis, technical strategist at Westpac, expects the contract to trade in a 93.360 to 93.440 range on the day with overbought conditions to still overhanging the market.
The 14-day relative strength index on the 10-year contract remains around 70 percent, although it is well below the recent plus-80 percent extreme overbought levels.

"(The 10-year bond is) looking expensive relative to New Zealand, and lesser extent to the U.S., and suggest with more U.S. weakness expected tonight that first support of 93.360/380 will not necessarily hold," Pontikis added.

The U.S. market continued its softer pre-weekend trend on Monday ahead of what is expected to be a hawkish commentary by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan in his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

However, analysts expect there will be a reluctance to sell the local market too heavily just yet with this Wednesday's second quarter inflation report forecast to be extremely benign. The report could trigger a further easing in monetary policy as long as Thursday's second quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings do not contain any surprises.
